scope: First school Maths mock: AQA Year 1/AS Pure only; no Year 2, Mechanics or Statistics.
rationale: The existing 138-question first-mock Pure bank contains v190 and v191 proof, vector and transformations questions. Additional independent multi-step applications are useful, but this does not prove a specification gap or mastery.

newOriginalQuestions.challenge: Proof n⁵−n divisible by 30 using deduction and five residue classes
Counterexample to an all-prime claim and general parity proof
Parameterized collinearity, AB:BC and exact unit vector
Midpoint theorem, parallel lines and exact 2D magnitude
Reflected shifted quadratic, exact turning point and intercepts

marker.mode: Dedicated independent maths-as-pure-marking-v209.js rules, no generic token-overlap fallback
marker.limit: Only the tested answer variants and specific rules are calibrated; handwritten and unfamiliar correct methods may require manual score adjustment.

protections: No edits to the 3345-card core deck or 1268-question master bank
No changed flashcard or existing question IDs
No changes to stored progress/profile/settings keys or cloud sync
No Year 2 Maths, Mechanics or Statistics in first-mock question pool
limitations: No historical AQA paper questions copied or verified by this version.
Task 1 specification-by-specification coverage remains unaudited to completion.
No claim that scoring matches an official AQA examiner for all responses.
Check official AQA specification and school mock scope again if teacher changes the assessed topics.
